issues.title: Support platform-owned installers and explicit application recovery
issues.evidence: Configured lifecycle commands can invoke platform installers. SuiFleet must preserve execution state and accurately report supplied results across daemon/device restarts without owning OS installation, partitions, reboot or firmware recovery.
acceptance: Deliver verified artifacts to explicitly configured lifecycle commands, including platform installer scripts; do not autodetect or select an updater, require A/B partitions, or prescribe an OS-update architecture.
Platform scripts/tools own OS installation, reboot decisions, boot confirmation and firmware rollback. SuiFleet must not initiate reboot or implement a firmware boot/recovery state machine.

Preserve SuiFleet execution/journal state across platform-controlled restarts; distinguish command completion from interrupted/unknown work and record only results explicitly supplied by configured commands or platform reporting. Never infer successful boot from exit zero or automatically repeat ambiguous destructive work.

For application components, persist last-known-good versions/configuration and perform previous-version rollback through explicitly configured lifecycle/recovery commands when deployment or health checks fail. Test the resulting component version and state. This application-only rollback does not authorize OS installation, system reboot or firmware rollback.

Demonstrate a configured installer handoff with a harmless fixture and, on a supported platform, an installer-script integration. Platform-specific physical recovery evidence documents that integration and is not a universal prerequisite for SuiFleet lifecycle infrastructure.
issues.validation: Artifact-integrity and configured-command handoff tests; daemon restart/interrupted-work journal tests; explicit-result and application-recovery tests. Record platform installer integration separately. No implicit updater detection, SuiFleet-triggered reboot or mandatory A/B acceptance.
issues.description: Support verified artifact delivery and configured lifecycle commands for platform-owned installers such as SWUpdate or RAUC. issues.title: Require Seal-encrypted artifact delivery and scoped decryption for customer readiness
issues.evidence: Current artifact uploads send original bytes and recipe JSON to Walrus; hashes and deployment authority do not provide confidentiality. The user explicitly requires Seal encryption and scoped access as a commercial prototype/customer-readiness baseline.
acceptance: Encrypt proprietary artifacts and confidential recipe/configuration content client-side before any publisher/relay/Walrus upload. Default the customer-facing path to confidential delivery; allow clearly labeled explicit public artifacts for public/open-source tests. Never silently fall back to plaintext.

Define versioned Seal policy identities for releases/artifacts and explicit account/device/group decryption scopes. An authorized administrator grants/revokes access with signed onchain transactions; recipients use their own keys. Enforce publish/deploy/admin operations separately through actual Move authority, not frontend visibility or possession of a decryption key. Document any role/capability transfer and delegation semantics.

Implement unattended edge Seal authentication with its own enrolled device signer and bounded session credentials, including correct personal-message/session signing for supported software/hardware signers. Never copy the administrator wallet seed, recovery phrase or private key to an edge client or require an administrator signature per download. Keep private keys local to their signer.

Check active device identity and policy scope before key release; validate configured key-server identities and transport. Include device/group authorization, removal, revoked/rotated identities, policy/package upgrades and old-policy namespace bypass attempts. Do not promise atomic revocation across asynchronously observed chain state.

Decrypt locally with bounded resource use and verify authenticated encryption plus the defined artifact/recipe digests before execution. Specify which metadata/digests are public and ciphertext-versus-plaintext binding. Never log/cache plaintext confidential data or reusable decryption keys outside explicitly protected runtime/cache paths.

Define key/session lifetime, rotation, offline caching/expiry and disk cleanup. State that previously obtained plaintext or decryption keys cannot be remotely revoked; fresh protected versions need suitable new encryption identities/keys. Define whether offline execution is permitted and the resulting revocation limitation.

Choose and validate suitable production key providers/authentication, fees, availability and recovery; provider API credentials are distinct from device identity and must not be baked into public frontend assets/images. Respect Seal documented data-sensitivity exclusions; no unqualified KMS/HSM/regulated-data claims.

Provide reproducible encrypted upload -> authorized edge decryption/application -> onchain result acceptance and unauthorized-account/device, tamper, wrong-network/policy, expiry, keyserver outage, rotation/revocation and offline-cache failures. Public OTA smoke tests may proceed earlier but do not establish confidential customer readiness.
issues.validation: Move policy/authority and upgrade tests; frontend typecheck/build with verified pre-upload encryption; Rust signer/session/decryption tests and encrypted OTA simulator; authorized public-testnet encrypted delivery/effects checks. Track real extension-wallet/Pi acceptance separately in SF-010/SF-031. Record actual key-provider/network costs and limitations; no plaintext fallback or administrator secret distribution.
issues.description: Implement Seal-based encryption before Walrus upload and authenticated, policy-scoped edge decryption. This is required before claiming readiness for proprietary customer deployments; intentionally public test artifacts remain an explicit mode. Existing deployment/admin authority remains enforced separately by Move capabilities and roles.

issues.title: Prepay fleet network costs up front and fund devices through an on-chain gas float
issues.description:
The person using the dApp pays all fleet network costs up front: device gas for receipts and data anchors, and Walrus/Seal storage for artifacts, telemetry and logs. Design (user decision 2026-10-19): an on-chain gas float. The owner deposits into a fleet budget contract; at registration the dApp funds the device's address with a small capped float, and devices top up from the budget only through the contract, within on-chain limits. No server, gas station or sponsoring key; Walrus storage is drawn from owner-prepaid storage held by the contract, and the resulting blobs are fleet-owned. Compromised devices are a primary threat: every limit must bound what a fully compromised device can spend, write or destroy.

Payment-failure integration — user requirement: https://github.com/tyler-suifleet/suifleet/issues/179
issues.evidence: Devices currently need their own SUI for every receipt; the only allowance today is the CI testnet runner's (docs/TESTNET.md). User direction 2026-10-19: network costs are paid up front by whoever uses the app; use the on-chain float now, not a server-side gas station. Sui sponsored transactions need a live sponsor signature (an always-on signer); Nautilus enclaves are self-managed AWS instances, so both were rejected for now and recorded as future options.

Gas float: device registration funds the device address with at most a configured float; top-ups only through the contract, never above the float cap or the period allowance. Document that SUI already held by a device cannot be clawed back, so loss from a compromised device is bounded by its float plus one period allowance.

Owner-prepaid Walrus storage held by the contract: a device's upload takes only the storage it needs within its quota, the blob is registered under fleet ownership (the device cannot delete or shorten fleet history), and storage rebates return to the owner. Verify Storage splitting and blob wrapping against a pinned Walrus version before building on them.

Compromised-device controls: revocation stops all draws immediately; a fleet-wide pause; per-device rate limits; dApp alerts for devices drawing at their limits or anomalously; draw and upload calls exist only in the current package, with old-package entry points proven unable to draw (old-package attack tests).

Key isolation: the SF-053 signing service signs draw transactions only for the budget contract, within the configured amounts, and only for the daemon's main process; a compromised component cannot request draws, and a compromised daemon remains bounded by the on-chain limits.

The dApp shows an up-front estimate (devices, receipt and data cadence, artifact and data storage) from measured SF-054 costs, asks the user to approve the deposit, shows balance and per-device usage, warns before exhaustion, and supports top-up and withdrawal of unused funds.
Show on-ramp and swap fees, regional availability limits and the final network-cost deposit separately in the estimate before the user approves.

Users can pay in SUI only: the deposit transaction swaps the WAL portion through a pinned, verified Sui DEX route in the same transaction with slippage limits, or the dApp explains why a direct WAL purchase is required.

Card payment without a server: embed a fiat on-ramp's hosted checkout (prefer providers that sell WAL, currently Coinbase or OnRamp.money per Sui's on-ramp list), pre-filled with the user's wallet address, asset and amount; KYC stays inside the provider's flow; no provider webhooks or server-side APIs.

issues.title: Cut daemon chain reads to one batched read per poll
issues.description: Make the daemon's steady-state poll a single BatchGetObjects version check instead of ~23 to ~45 separate gRPC reads, so a 1,000-device fleet can run on Mysten's public full node and later on one shared node. This is Stage 1 of the low-cost Sui-only product in docs/BUSINESS_PLAN.md (pricing proposal 2026-10-23).
issues.evidence: Code review of main e19970e (2026-10-23): with a budget and one group, each 10 s poll makes 21+2G reads: validate_deployment 4 (sui_client.rs:289-345), validate_cap 3 (sui_client.rs:847-875), funding::top_up 4 (funding.rs:248-250), deployments() 2 (sui_client.rs:484-520) and reconcile 2+3+2G+3 (linux_main.rs:1064-1095). fleet_data health adds 10 reads (fleet_data.rs:145-182) and the archive tick 12 (fleet_archive.rs:122-144), refetching the whole package (sui_client.rs:1148-1158). That is ~11.7B reads and ~39 TB of RPC traffic a month for 1,000 devices, which forces dedicated full nodes ($0.78-2.29/device/month). One device alone exceeds Mysten's documented public-endpoint guidance of 100 requests per 30 s (docs.sui.io/references/sui-api/rpc-best-practices). acceptance: Cache immutables per manifest: package bytes and type origins, registry type and initial shared version, and chain identity; invalidate only when the manifest changes.

Any version change or NotFound triggers the existing full validation, which still fails closed.

Event discovery runs on the slow path only (a watched version changed, or a bounded interval): one ListEvents DNF query for DeploymentCreated and DeviceAddedToGroup with a local creator/target pre-filter, preserving the reconcile double-read guarantee, with a tested one-time merge of the two journal cursors.
fleet_data health and archive loops sleep until due without validation reads; the diagnostic-request read joins the version batch. Gas top-up reads balance and budget only immediately before a write.
A full revalidation still runs at a configurable bound (default daily). Revocation, key rotation, package upgrade and chain-reset detection are no slower than one poll interval.
Instrument and report reads and bytes per poll before and after, on the OTA simulator and localnet.
issues.validation: cargo test plus make test-ota; localnet tests proving revocation, rotation, upgrade and chain reset still fail closed under caching; a read-count test asserting one request per steady-state poll; bounded testnet run under docs/TESTNET.md.

issues.title: Remove client/server hydration mismatches from the console pages
issues.description: On main 0ca16547 every console route except Data and Device services throws 'Hydration failed because the server rendered text/HTML didn't match the client. As a result this tree will be regenerated on the client' on load (12 of 14 routes, logged out and connected). React discards the server-rendered tree and renders again, which doubles initial work, flashes content and hides genuine render bugs behind the regenerated tree. The static export must hydrate cleanly.
issues.evidence: 2026-10-26 UI-only evaluation at main 2283fc99 (seal-testnet profile, agent wallet 0x0e4994…6965); re-checked 2026-10-27 at main 0ca16547. Headless Chrome re-check on 0ca16547 (dev server, testnet profile) recorded one hydration page error on each of /, /get-started, /devices, /enrollment, /deployments, /rollouts, /components, /firmware, /access, /handover, /settings and /budget; the 2283fc99 build showed none. Texts are in the evaluation journal comment on SF-170.
acceptance: Loading each console route from the production static export produces no hydration warnings or errors in the browser console, logged out and with a connected wallet.

Values that legitimately differ between server and client (locale dates, wallet state, storage-backed state, network label) render through a mounted/client-only path or an explicitly commented suppressHydrationWarning, not by disabling server rendering wholesale.
An automated check (Playwright or jsdom) loads every route of the built export and fails on any hydration error; it runs in CI.
issues.validation: make dapp-typecheck, make dapp-build, the new per-route hydration check in CI; manual load of each route in the static export with and without a wallet.

issues.title: Make dashboard tiles count reported health and admitting deployments only
issues.description: The dashboard tile 'Devices (healthy)' shows 1 for a registered device that has never reported and that the Devices page labels 'Health unavailable'; when no health reporting is configured the tile falls back to the registered-device count under the 'healthy' label. 'Active deployments' shows 2 while one of the two deployments is paused ('Paused; resume to admit waiting devices'). An on-call engineer reading the headline numbers would believe every device is healthy and every deployment admitting.
issues.evidence: 2026-10-26 UI-only evaluation at main 2283fc99 (seal-testnet profile, agent wallet 0x0e4994…6965); re-checked 2026-10-27 at main 0ca16547. Tiles read 'DEVICES (HEALTHY) 1' and 'ACTIVE DEPLOYMENTS 2' on both builds with device lab-gateway-01 'Health unavailable', 'Last seen never' and the 9:46 PM deployment paused (evaluation Step 33; re-check texts on SF-170). dapp/src/app/page.tsx renders devices.length when reported is false and pending.length as active.
acceptance: Without health reporting the tile is labelled as a registered-device count with a 'health not reported' hint and never implies health; with reporting it shows healthy versus total.
'Active deployments' counts only deployments that can admit devices (not paused, cancelled, expired or complete); paused deployments are shown separately or in the hint.
Unit tests cover unreported, partially reported and paused cases.
issues.validation: dapp unit tests for the tile derivations; make dapp-typecheck and make dapp-build; manual check against a testnet fleet with one paused deployment.

issues.title: Build staged rollouts from library versions and named cohorts
issues.description: 'Create a gradual rollout' requires typing component, version, recipe blob ID, artifactSha256 and recipeSha256 by hand, cohorts as space-separated device object IDs, every duration in milliseconds (rate window, bake period, stall timeout) and the failure threshold in basis points. After creation nothing confirms success until the page is reloaded; the Members list shows object IDs instead of device names; 'Check device health and continue' advanced the decision counter from 1 to 2 with Granted still 0 of 1 and no explanation of the outcome. The headline Greengrass-replacement feature currently reads as an internal test harness.
issues.evidence: 2026-10-26 UI-only evaluation at main 2283fc99 (seal-testnet profile, agent wallet 0x0e4994…6965); re-checked 2026-10-27 at main 0ca16547. Evaluation Steps 27–30: rollout 0xa909b8f1…3b19, create digest J6hPNC4i…, advance digest C7ZxwDtS…. On 0ca16547 the labels are unchanged (component, version, recipe, artifactSha256, recipeSha256, Cohorts, 'Rate window (ms)', 'Bake period (ms)', 'Stall timeout before pause (ms)'), the member line reads 'Cohort 1 · 0x913cdd67… · Waiting' and the panel 'Active · cohort 1 · decision 2' with Granted 0 of 1.
acceptance: The form selects a published library version (or a direct upload's recipe) and fills the recipe blob ID and both digests from it; manual entry stays available under an advanced section with digest validation.
Cohorts are built from device groups and named devices (search, multi-select, reorder) and shown by name with object IDs on demand; the immutable-snapshot semantics are explained next to the builder.
Durations are entered in seconds, minutes or hours and the failure threshold as a percentage; the exact policy values are shown in a review step before signing.

Creating a rollout shows a confirmed result (digest and link to the panel) without a reload, and every advance or evaluate decision reports its outcome in words: devices admitted, why none were admitted, and what must happen next.
Members and decision lists show device names; the manual-approval model ('return here to approve each step') is stated on the create screen.
issues.validation: dapp unit tests for form-to-transaction mapping and outcome messages; make dapp-typecheck and make dapp-build; one testnet rollout created from a library version under the standing grant, digests and cost recorded.

issues.title: Keep rollout decision audits readable from current chain state
issues.description: The rollout panel's Decision audit reads RolloutDecision events by paging listEvents on the public fullnode. Public nodes prune event history: two minutes after creating a rollout the panel reported 'Decision history unavailable: requested data below earliest available; lowest available checkpoint is 394124393', and the same rollout the next day reports lowest available checkpoint 394277063. The audited health gate exists on chain, but operators on the supported public-RPC configuration cannot read their own audit trail, and the persistent 'some history may be missing' status offers nothing they can act on. Under the no-server strategy (SF-137) the audit must be readable without an archival endpoint.
issues.evidence: 2026-10-26 UI-only evaluation at main 2283fc99 (seal-testnet profile, agent wallet 0x0e4994…6965); re-checked 2026-10-27 at main 0ca16547. Evaluation Step 31 and the 0ca16547 re-check (rollout 0xa909b8f1…3b19 at decision 2). Reader: fetchRolloutDecisions in dapp/src/lib/rollout-progress.ts (listEvents descending, 20 pages); warnings from dapp/src/lib/event-history.ts.
acceptance: Each rollout's decisions (revision, time, state, cohort, reason, admitted IDs) are readable from current object state or fleet-owned storage, for example a bounded on-chain decision log on the rollout record or a Walrus batch indexed from it, independent of fullnode event retention; contract changes are additive and upgrade-safe.
The panel shows the full decision history where it exists and states exactly which revisions are unreadable for rollouts created before the change.
The Data status indicator distinguishes history pruned by this connection from complete history, links to the connection explanation and never stacks duplicate warnings.
Move tests cover the decision log bounds; dapp tests cover reading and rendering; an upgrade test shows existing rollouts keep working.
issues.validation: make test-contracts, dapp unit tests, make dapp-typecheck and make dapp-build; an automatic testnet upgrade and rollout run under the standing grant that reads the audit after the fullnode's lowest checkpoint has advanced past the decision.

issues.title: Choose, show and extend a release's storage period inside the publish flow
issues.description: Publishing a version never asks how long the release must stay downloadable. The wallet-paid path silently uses the build's NEXT_PUBLIC_WALRUS_EPOCHS (5 epochs, about 5 days on testnet), the review step says nothing about expiry, and the success message prints 'storage expires at epoch N' together with a literal 'walrus extend --blob-obj-id … --epochs-extended 5' command-line instruction the app never introduced. A device that comes online after expiry cannot fetch the update, and the only remedy is a tool outside the product.
issues.evidence: 2026-10-26 UI-only evaluation at main 2283fc99 (seal-testnet profile, agent wallet 0x0e4994…6965); re-checked 2026-10-27 at main 0ca16547. Evaluation Step 20: version 0x5fc4aea7…12c1 with blobs expiring at epoch 568. On 0ca16547 wizard steps 2 and 3 still contain no storage-period field or expiry notice for wallet-paid uploads; ComponentPublisher still emits storage warnings and renewalCommand from dapp/src/lib/walrus.ts; only the fleet-paid FleetStorageChoice shows retention.
acceptance: The publish wizard, the Greengrass import and the Deploy component upload show the storage period in days with its price, defaulting from fleet settings where configured, and let the operator change it before signing; the review step states the expiry date.
Library and deployment screens show each version's expiry and warn ahead of it (for example 7 days before), including for versions still targeted by desired state or active deployments.
Extending storage is an in-app action (wallet-paid or fleet-paid) and no customer screen prints a command-line instruction.
Offline tests cover the period and price computation, the warnings and the extend transaction builder.
issues.validation: dapp unit tests; make dapp-typecheck and make dapp-build; one testnet publish with a chosen period plus one in-app extension under the standing grant, WAL and SUI cost recorded.

issues.title: Publish through alternative Walrus publishers when the configured one fails
issues.description: Every upload goes to the single publisher URL in the deployment manifest. During the evaluation the public testnet publisher (publisher.walrus-testnet.walrus.space) returned HTTP 500 'could not find WAL coins with sufficient balance'; the wizard printed the raw JSON body and stopped, with no in-app way to choose another publisher. Firmware distribution was impossible until the deployment manifest was edited by hand on the vendor side. Other public publishers answered at the same time (one succeeded, two returned 502).
issues.evidence: 2026-10-26 UI-only evaluation at main 2283fc99 (seal-testnet profile, agent wallet 0x0e4994…6965); re-checked 2026-10-27 at main 0ca16547. Evaluation Steps 16–19. On 0ca16547 the manifest still carries one walrus.publisher_url and one aggregator_url (profiles/seal-testnet/frontend.env); Fleet settings has no storage endpoint control; the fleet-paid SDK path (dapp/src/lib/fleet-upload.ts) needs a fleet_storage deployment that the hosted testnet fleet lacks (SF-173).
acceptance: The deployment manifest accepts an ordered list of publisher and aggregator URLs; uploads fail over to the next publisher on 5xx or network errors and reads fail over across aggregators, recording which endpoint served each blob; single-URL manifests keep working.
Publisher failures are shown in plain language (what failed, which endpoint, what the operator can do) with the raw response under technical details.

An operator can add a publisher URL for the session or the fleet from the console, validated and stored without rebuilding the app, and the fleet-paid SDK path is chosen automatically when fleet storage is configured.
Offline tests cover failover order, exhausted publishers and error rendering; no test mocks a success the publisher did not return.
issues.validation: dapp unit tests with simulated publisher responses; make dapp-typecheck and make dapp-build; one testnet publish through a secondary publisher under the standing grant.

issues.title: Accept canonical Greengrass recipe casing and report every import finding at once
issues.description: The Greengrass importer rejects recipes written the way AWS documents them: lifecycle keys must be lowercase install/run/shutdown (AWS examples use Install/Run/Shutdown) and the artifact key must be Uri (AWS uses URI). Findings arrive one layer per check: casing and configuration first, then configuration interpolation and unbound s3:// URIs, so a typical recipe needs three check cycles. Rejecting bootstrap, startup and recover with guidance is acceptable; the casing rule makes every existing recipe require hand editing.
issues.evidence: 2026-10-26 UI-only evaluation at main 2283fc99 (seal-testnet profile, agent wallet 0x0e4994…6965); re-checked 2026-10-27 at main 0ca16547. Evaluation Steps 18–19. On 0ca16547 the same two-manifest recipe is 'Rejected' with unknown-lifecycle-step ('Lifecycle step names are exact lowercase install, run or shutdown'), unsupported-artifact-key ('Artifacts may contain only Uri, Unarchive, Permission, Digest and Algorithm') and configuration-without-command.
acceptance: Lifecycle step names and artifact keys are matched case-insensitively as AWS does (Install/Run/Shutdown, URI/Uri), with the canonical spelling shown in the translated manifest; duplicates differing only by case are rejected with a message.

One 'Check translation' reports all findings for the recipe (structure, casing, configuration, interpolation, artifacts) in a single list, so a correct recipe needs at most one artifact-binding round.
docs/GREENGRASS_COMPATIBILITY.md and the in-app guidance state the accepted spellings; translation tests gain AWS-cased fixtures.
issues.validation: greengrass-recipe unit tests with AWS-documented recipe fixtures; make dapp-typecheck and make dapp-build.

issues.title: Deploy library versions as a group's desired version
issues.description: The direct Deploy component route sets a group's desired version by default (devices converge, late joiners receive it, removed devices stop following), but 'Deploy this version' from the software library says 'Catalog versions deploy one-shot; desired state does not select them yet'. The publish-once/deploy-many route therefore loses the convergence model that makes group deployments safe, which is backwards for operators who keep an immutable library.
issues.evidence: 2026-10-26 UI-only evaluation at main 2283fc99 (seal-testnet profile, agent wallet 0x0e4994…6965); re-checked 2026-10-27 at main 0ca16547. Evaluation Steps 21–22 (deployment digest 8vigsDjA…). On 0ca16547 /firmware/?componentVersion=0x5fc4aea7…12c1 still shows the one-shot note (dapp/src/app/firmware/page.tsx).
acceptance: Desired state can reference a catalog version with multi-platform manifests so a group converges on a library version exactly as on a direct upload; the daemon selects its platform manifest from the version.
The library deploy screen offers the desired-state checkbox with the same semantics and copy as the direct route; one-shot stays available.
Contract and daemon changes are additive and upgrade-safe; Move, daemon and simulator tests cover catalog-backed desired state, platform selection and supersession.
issues.validation: make test-contracts, make edge-test, make test-ota, make dapp-typecheck and make dapp-build; automatic testnet acceptance of a catalog-backed desired-state deployment under the standing grant.

issues.title: Show new operators where to get, install and configure the device client
issues.description: Nothing in the console says where the SuiFleet device client comes from, how to install it or what it needs. Get started says 'Start the SuiFleet client on the device and copy the device address it displays'; the register form wants 'the device's own address from the daemon'; Enrollment is the first place the binary name and 'suifleet --enroll' appear. A prospect cannot complete the first-device flow without leaving the product to search for documentation the app never links.

The device-address step explains how the client prints the address and what the operator should see.
Links resolve to published documentation (repository docs until the SF-172 site exists) and a link-check test covers them.

issues.title: Assign many devices to groups in one transaction
issues.description: Group membership changes happen one device per wallet approval in the Manage group dialog; the only bulk route is the default group at enrollment. Moving or adding hundreds of already-enrolled devices (a new site, a new canary set) is not viable one transaction at a time.
issues.evidence: 2026-10-26 UI-only evaluation at main 2283fc99 (seal-testnet profile, agent wallet 0x0e4994…6965); re-checked 2026-10-27 at main 0ca16547. Evaluation Step 10 (member add digest 9enxVruL…); the dialog is unchanged on 0ca16547.
acceptance: The Devices page supports selecting devices (filter, search, or a pasted list of serials or names) and adding them to or removing them from one or more groups in batched transactions with a bounded size, after a review of the changes and the number of approvals needed.
Partial failures report exactly which devices changed; nothing is retried blindly.
Contract entry points stay additive; Move and dapp tests cover batch limits and architecture mismatches.
issues.validation: make test-contracts, dapp unit tests, make dapp-typecheck and make dapp-build; one testnet batch of at least three devices under the standing grant.

issues.title: Launch the suifleet.io landing site with app link, guided walkthrough and videos
issues.description: SuiFleet has no public entry point beyond the hosted console. Prospects need a landing site at suifleet.io that explains the product, links to the app, carries a step-by-step guide with short videos (sign in, fund, register a device, enroll a batch, publish a version, deploy to a group, run a staged rollout), documentation, pricing from the business plan, security and custody notes, and contact details. This follows the usual structure for Sui and other crypto applications: a static marketing site on the apex domain, the app on app.<domain>, documentation on docs.<domain>, and no application server.
issues.evidence: User request on 2026-10-27 after the outsider evaluation; the evaluation found no in-product path to documentation or to the device client (SF-169).
acceptance: A static site source (for example under site/) builds reproducibly with pages for home (value proposition, 'Launch app'), how it works, the guide with embedded videos, pricing, documentation entry, security and custody, and contact/privacy; no tracking scripts without consent.
Each guide step matches the current console build and has a screencast recorded on testnet with no credentials or keys visible, reproducible from a checklist or script kept in the repository.

The hosting and DNS plan for suifleet.io, app.suifleet.io and docs.suifleet.io is documented, including whether the site is served from conventional static hosting or Walrus Sites, and the release process joins the release runbook.
Build and link checks run in CI; publication to the live domain requires explicit user authorization and is recorded separately.
issues.validation: site build and link check in CI; manual review of every page and video; no production publication without the user's go-ahead.

issues.title: Deploy the complete fleet stack on the hosted testnet evaluation fleet
issues.description: The hosted testnet console (seal-testnet profile) runs a deployment whose manifest has only the registry object. Network budget says 'Shared fleet funding is not available in this setup', Data and the publish wizard say 'Prepaid Walrus storage is not configured for this build (no fleet_storage package)', Device services says 'This fleet is not connected to the reporting service', Fleet settings cannot be saved ('not available in this fleet configuration') and health never reports. A prospect evaluating from the hosted app sees roughly a third of the product switched off.
issues.evidence: 2026-10-26 UI-only evaluation at main 2283fc99 (seal-testnet profile, agent wallet 0x0e4994…6965); re-checked 2026-10-27 at main 0ca16547. Evaluation Steps 4, 15, 32 and 33; on 0ca16547 the profiles/seal-testnet/frontend.env manifest lists registry as its only shared object and the quoted copy appears on /budget, /data, /services and /settings.
acceptance: The evaluation fleet on testnet has fleet budget, fleet storage, fleet settings, data config and health reporting deployed and recorded in its deployment manifest, under the standing testnet grant and spend limits; package publishes are cached and identical code is never republished.
The hosted console points at that manifest and every 'not configured for this build' message disappears on the evaluation fleet; a documented script reproduces the setup.
Funding levels in SUI and WAL and a top-up procedure for the evaluation fleet are documented with costs recorded; no mainnet or production credentials are involved.

issues.title: Recurring maintenance windows for deployments
issues.description: Deployments support a single one-off window (window start and end) plus not-before, expiry and advance notice. Fleet operators with site rules such as 'Sundays 02:00–04:00 local time' need recurring windows interpreted in the site's timezone. Greengrass does not offer this natively, so this is an opportunity rather than parity; it is recorded from the evaluation for product review before any implementation is scheduled.
issues.evidence: 2026-10-26 UI-only evaluation at main 2283fc99 (seal-testnet profile, agent wallet 0x0e4994…6965); re-checked 2026-10-27 at main 0ca16547. Evaluation Step 24; the schedule editor is unchanged on 0ca16547.
acceptance: A product decision is recorded (scope, per-device timezone source, on-chain representation) before implementation starts; if declined, the ticket closes with the reason in the business or design documents.

If approved: a deployment can carry a recurring weekly window with a timezone that the daemon evaluates locally and reports as a deferral reason; the editor shows the next three admission windows; contract and daemon changes are additive and tested.
issues.validation: Move, daemon and simulator tests for recurring window evaluation; make dapp-typecheck and make dapp-build.
